name: Nomatsiguenga
confidence_why: Shaver 1996 (a dictionary appendix credited largely to David Payne) describes the accented vowel as marked by high pitch rather than length or loudness, but Apolinario 2020, the only acoustic study (72 nouns, six speakers), finds a duration-cued stress confined to the first two syllables of the noun (penultimate by default) with the lexical high tone a separate, non-obligatory system and states outright that Nomatsigenga is not a pitch accent language, while Lawrence 2013, known only through Apolinario's summary, also separates tone from stress yet places the stress on the final syllable of disyllables, so both the type of system and the position of the accent remain contested among the three descriptions.

catalog_quote: Se puede decir que el nomatsiguenga posee acento tonal, es decir que las palabras pueden tener ciertas vocales marcadas con un acento. La vocal acentuada se pronuncia con un tono bastante mas alto que las demas vocales de la palabra. La vocal acentuada no es siempre mas larga ni mas fuerte que las demas que aparecen en la palabra; en efecto, las vocales no acentuadas pueden pronunciarse con m&s fuerza (o mas intensidad) que la vocal acentuada. ... Puesto que la vocal acentuada se distingue principalmente por el tono alto, y no por la intensidad (mayor fuerza de la voz) o por la duracion, resulta mas correcto hablar de "acento tonal" que de "acento prosodico" o de "tono". Algunos pares de palabras difieren solamente por el acento tonal. Por ejemplo: yogacaro el lo tomo (bebió) yogacaro el lo guardo / pomoro paloma grande pomoro caracol grande / pero luciernaga pero siempre. Las raices su…
sweep_summary: One works with stress in the title, already held by the project and now read in full: Apolinario Vilcarromero 2020 (UNMSM Licenciatura thesis, open PDF via Biblioteca Digital Curt Nimuendajú / etnolinguistica.org). It is squarely about word stress in Nomatsigenga nouns and contradicts the catalog's 'tonal' coding (Shaver 1996 dictionary appendix, 'acento tonal'): stress is a duration-cued metrical system in a left-edge two-syllable window (penult in 72% incl. all disyllables; antepenult/initial in 25% of trisyllables; final in 2 words), CVN codas weightless, H tone a separate non-obligatory system, hence 'nomatsigenga no es una lengua pitch accent' (p. 89). Recommend reclassification the catalog from 'tonal' to a stress language with a left two-syllable window (penult default, lexically antepenult), citing Apolinario 2020 as deciding source and retaining Shaver/Lawrence for the H-tone contrast. Lawrence 2013 (UT Austin MA report, stress statement pp. 15-17) remains unfetchable (CloudFront 403; archive.org unreachable) and is the one acquisition worth pursuing.

new_statements.quote: El patrón acentual que gobierna los nombres de la lengua nomatsigenga consiste en asignar el acento dentro una ventana de las dos primeras sílabas dentro de la palabra nominal. [...] El primer patrón consiste en acentuar la antepenúltima sílaba. El segundo patrón, el más frecuente, señala que se debe acentuar la penúltima sílaba. [...] Los correlatos fonéticos principales del acento nominal son la duración y la calidad vocálica. Por tanto, nomatsigenga no es una lengua pitch accent, pues no todas sus sílabas acentuadas portan un tono alto.
new_statements.translation: The stress pattern governing nouns in Nomatsigenga consists in assigning stress within a window of the first two syllables of the noun. [...] The first pattern stresses the antepenultimate syllable. The second pattern, the most frequent, stresses the penultimate syllable. [...] The main phonetic correlates of nominal stress are duration and vowel quality. Therefore Nomatsigenga is not a pitch-accent language, since not all of its stressed syllables carry a high tone.
new_statements.citation: Apolinario Vilcarromero, Rosa Beatriz. 2020. Acento nominal en nomatsigenga (arawak). Tesis de Licenciatura, Universidad Nacional Mayor de San Marcos, Lima. 114 pp.
new_statements.locator: Conclusiones, printed p. 89 = p. 101 (supporting data: sec. 7.3 pp. 80-85, Tabla 45 p. 88, Tabla 18 p. 60)
new_statements.reading: First-hand acoustic and metrical study (72 nouns, 6 speakers) finds a genuine stress system, cued by duration and vowel quality, confined to the first two syllables of the noun: penultimate in 72% of words (all disyllables, most trisyllables), antepenultimate/initial in 25% of trisyllables, final in 2 words; CVN codas are weightless; the H-tone contrast reported by Shaver/Lawrence coexists but is not obligatory on the stressed syllable. This directly contradicts the catalog's 'tonal' (pitch accent) coding built on Shaver 1996's dictionary appendix, which had no phonetic backing. Caveats: nouns only, 2-3 syllable words only, Licenciatura thesis; the tone contrast itself is not denied.

new_statements.quote: Nomatsigenga has a contrast between high tone and no tone, as shown in the minimal pair in (2.18-2.19), where the only difference in the two words is the tone on the vowel root. [...] The placement of tone on the word is not predictable and is assigned to each syllable individually. [...] This distinction suggests that the tone bearing unit is the mora, not the syllable. Barring any special stress-attracting syllables, stress is assigned in disyllabic iambic feet, with main word stress on the final foot. Stress is attracted to closed syllables and those that are assigned high tone. Some clitics, such as the first- and second-person object markers, =na and =mi, carry inherent stress.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Two coexisting systems: (i) a lexical, unpredictable privative tone contrast (H vs no tone; TBU = mora; one true minimal pair); (ii) word stress assigned by disyllabic iambic feet with main stress on the final (rightmost) foot, overridden by stress-attracting syllables: closed (N-coda) syllables, syllables with true diphthongs /ai oi ei/ (but not /ëi/), and H-toned syllables attract stress; object clitics =na, =mi are inherently stressed. Transcribed examples (p. 12-13): notsoigani [no.ˈtsoi.ˌga.ni], aisáti [ˌai.ˈsá.ti], ikampëna [i.ˌkam.pë.ˈna], yamëka [ˈya.më.ka].
new_statements.secondary_stress: Secondary stresses are transcribed on non-head feet / heavy syllables (e.g. [no.ˈtsoi.ˌga.ni], [ˌai.ˈsá.ti], [i.ˌkam.pë.ˈna]) but no explicit rule for secondary stress is stated beyond 'main word stress on the final foot'.
new_statements.exceptions: Diphthongs /ai, oi, ei/ attract stress regardless of position while phonetic diphthong /ëi/ (orthographic ë) does not (p. 12); closed syllables and H-toned syllables attract stress; clitics =na and =mi carry inherent stress (p. 17-18); /h/-deletion yields H tone on an adjacent stressed vowel (p. 20). The sketch is brief (one paragraph on stress) with no acoustic measurement of stress; the report's topic is verbal morphology.
new_statements.identity_note: Lawrence 2013 is based on fieldwork in San Antonio de Sonomoro (Pangoa, Satipo, Junín), 2010-2012, ISO not; same language as the catalog entry, mostly verbal data. Apolinario 2020 studied nouns only (2-3 syllables). Part of the placement disagreement may reflect word class (verbs with clitics vs bare nouns) rather than dialect.

tone_statements.quote: De acuerdo con Shaver (1996) y Lawrence (2013), el nomatsigenga exhibe una distinción tonal (i.e., tono vs ausencia de tono). Obsérvese que en ningún ejemplo de la lengua en este documento el tono y/o los acentos están gráficamente marcados. Aún hace falta un estudio enfocado en la fonología suprasegmental de las palabras verbales. Apolinario (en preparación) presenta un estudio sobre el acento en nombres nomatsigenga. [...] Lawrence (2013) sostiene que la elisión de esta consonante genera un tono alto en una de las vocales contiguas a /h/.
tone_statements.translation: According to Shaver (1996) and Lawrence (2013), Nomatsigenga exhibits a tonal distinction (i.e., tone vs absence of tone). Note that in no example of the language in this document are tone and/or accents marked graphically. A study focused on the suprasegmental phonology of verbal words is still lacking. Apolinario (in preparation) presents a study of accent in Nomatsigenga nouns. [...] Lawrence (2013) holds that the elision of this consonant generates a high tone on one of the vowels adjacent to /h/.

readall_conflicts: Neither listed work could be opened, so no new first-hand statements were obtained; the overall reading stays with the existing first-hand statement (Apolinario 2020: duration-cued stress in a window of the first two syllables of the noun, penultimate in 72% of the 72 nouns and in all disyllables, antepenultimate in ~25% of trisyllables, H tone a separate non-obligatory system), which already contradicts the catalog's tonal/pitch accent coding built on Shaver 1996. One further disagreement is visible only second-hand: Apolinario (pp. 9-10) reports Lawrence 2013: 17 as analysing stress as disyllabic iambic feet with stress attracted by closed syllables carrying high tone (e.g. [a.'ro], i.e. final stress in disyllables), whereas Apolinario's own acoustic data put stress on the first syllable of every disyllable and find CVN codas weightless. Whether Lawrence's iambic claim is really final-oriented, and whether it covers nouns or only verbs, cannot be checked until the UT Austin PDF is obtained from a host that CloudFront does not block. The two first-hand sources now obtained by the project agree on type but not on placement. tone.quote: De acuerdo con Shaver (1996) y Lawrence (2013), el nomatsigenga exhibe una distinción tonal (i.e., tono vs ausencia de tono). Obsérvese que en ningún ejemplo de la lengua en este documento el tono y/o los acentos están gráficamente marcados. Aún hace falta un estudio enfocado en la fonología suprasegmental de las palabras verbales. Apolinario (en preparación) presenta un estudio sobre el acento en nombres nomatsigenga. [...] Lawrence (2013) sostiene que la elisión de esta consonante genera un tono alto en una de las vocales contiguas a /h/.

tone.translation: According to Shaver (1996) and Lawrence (2013), Nomatsigenga exhibits a tonal distinction (i.e., tone vs absence of tone). Note that in no example of the language in this document are tone and/or accents marked graphically. A study focused on the suprasegmental phonology of verbal words is still lacking. Apolinario (in preparation) presents a study of accent in Nomatsigenga nouns. [...] Lawrence (2013) holds that the elision of this consonant generates a high tone on one of the vowels adjacent to /h/.
